items.title: Conflicting evidence on whether templates improve what is written
items.whyItMatters: A before-after study reported large quality gains and a content analysis found almost none (claim c3); a trial built on documentation counts could reward tick boxes (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Measure note quality with a calibrated score alongside documentation, and include training and feedback in the intervention.

items.title: Outcomes a trial would need have never been measured here
items.whyItMatters: Quality rating, goal-concordant care and family reports all need local testing before a stepped-wedge trial depends on them.
items.opportunity: Test rater agreement, extraction time and family questionnaire response on two wards first.

items.title: Families of younger and poorer patients respond least
items.whyItMatters: A postal questionnaire reached about a third of families, fewer in deprived neighbourhoods (claim c5).
items.opportunity: Test telephone and online options and track response by neighbourhood deprivation.

items.title: Undated regional benchmark
items.whyItMatters: The regional report gives no period or year, so its 19 percent median cannot be compared over time.
items.opportunity: Use the hospital's own 2025 baseline and treat the regional figure as context only.

errorsFound: Documentation rates alone would count a note recording only resuscitation status as a conversation.
reevaluation: The evidence argues against going straight to a trial whose outcomes are untested; a feasibility study on two wards should come first.
summary: Four gaps; the conflict about note quality and the untested outcomes are high severity.
